quest.title: Where Lies the Path Home
quest.description: One day, you and Paimon run into an old friend at Sumeru's city gates...
quest.rewards_formatted: Adventure EXP x875, Mora x53900, Hero's Wit x6, Mystic Enhancement Ore x12

talks.objective: Go to the entrance of Sumeru City

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: It wouldn't hurt to take a look.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hmm, that's true. Okay, let's go take a look.

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: Alright, lead the way, little Fungus.

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: It appears it was in a hurry because of this unconscious Fungus.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hmm, seems like they might be family.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: So maybe this Fungus wanted to bring Nahida here to help its family member.

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: Probably. Although Fungi are simple creatures, they're very sensitive to elemental power.

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: Maybe it noticed me on my way back and thought I'd be able to help.

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: I'll take a look. I should be able to help if it's just a common illness...

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: Hmm?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: What is it, Nahida?

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: Strange... very strange...

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: This Fungus didn't develop from a spore. It's an elemental life-form.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh? An elemental life-form?

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: Yes. Although the Fungi you normally see are capable of using elemental powers, they're merely borrowing elemental power from nature around them.

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: As for this Fungus... It has elemental power flowing through it. Definitely not anything like your typical Fungus.

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: Exactly. This is very interesting, I've never seen anything like it.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: So this is a first, even for Nahida...

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: But that's not all... there's a large void within its elemental power.

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: The void is stopping the elemental power from flowing normally, which must be why it fainted.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: So do you think it'll wake up if we can fill the void?

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: Yes, and I just so happen to be good at this sort of thing. I'll see what I can do right away.

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: My power was compatible. Looks like everything is fine now.

response.speaker: Elemental Being: Floating Hydro Fungus
response.text: Lord of Dendro... Is it really the Lord of Dendro?

response.speaker: Elemental Being: Floating Hydro Fungus
response.text: Oh, I can't believe the Lord of Dendro saved me... Thank you, as well as the stranger and creature next to you.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Wah! It can talk!?

response.speaker: Elemental Being: Floating Hydro Fungus
response.text: Oh, I didn't expect such a strange creature to make a sound like that. Seems I'm just as shocked as you are.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: What!? Of course Paimon can talk! And Paimon isn't a strange creature — Paimon's just... Paimon!

response.speaker: Elemental Being: Floating Hydro Fungus
response.text: Hello, Paimon. I am not yet able to evaluate an organism's intelligence from its appearance. I will only know you are able to speak once you have spoken.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh, uh, well no need to take it seriously. It's no big deal...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: But does Paimon really look so dumb that people might think Paimon doesn't know how to talk?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: There's no need to start worrying about that all of a sudden...

response.speaker: Elemental Being: Floating Hydro Fungus
response.text: You misunderstand, Paimon. A mouth is used for eating, breathing, and other functions that are more important than speaking.

response.speaker: Elemental Being: Floating Hydro Fungus
response.text: So a creature may not speak, even if it has a mouth. I've never seen a creature like you before, so I dared not make the assumption that you could speak.

response.speaker: Elemental Being: Floating Hydro Fungus
response.text: Even if you do possess a number of human traits, it is still very common for creatures to have similar external forms but completely different interiors — just like Fungi and Slimes.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Did this Fungus study at the Akademiya...? It seems even more talkative than Paimon...

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: You're not a Fungus, are you?

response.speaker: Elemental Being: Floating Hydro Fungus
response.text: That's correct. This might be surprising to you, and I'm sure that you must have questions. Let's find somewhere else to talk.

response.speaker: Elemental Being: Floating Hydro Fungus
response.text: It might startle my fellow "family members" if I speak too much using this strange voice.

response.speaker: Elemental Being: Floating Hydro Fungus
response.text: It says that it's very thankful for your help.

choices.text: It only looks like a Fungus?

talks.objective: Speak with the strangely behaving Fungus

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: Give me a moment. I'll contact them right now.

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: That should do it.

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: It may take some time to find them, so let's wait for a bit.

dialogues.speaker: Elemental Being: Floating Hydro Fungus
dialogues.text: Thank you, Lord of Dendro. We all believe that you will keep your promises.

dialogues.speaker: Elemental Being: Floating Hydro Fungus
dialogues.text: The moment I saw you when I awoke, I had a feeling you were here because of the agreement.

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: Hmm? Agreement?

dialogues.speaker: Elemental Being: Floating Hydro Fungus
dialogues.text: You might not remember, but this is a prophecy that we deeply believe in... That the Lord of Dendro will bring us home once the catastrophe comes to an end.

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: Oh, I see... I—I'm sorry, there are also some blurry segments in my memory as well.

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: But I'm very concerned about your homeland. This is something I should help with, it's really no trouble to me at all.

dialogues.speaker: Elemental Being: Floating Hydro Fungus
dialogues.text: Would you all be willing to come with me somewhere as we wait?

dialogues.speaker: Elemental Being: Floating Hydro Fungus
dialogues.text: The more family members that can return home with me... the better...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: But didn't you say that you don't know where they are?

dialogues.speaker: Elemental Being: Floating Hydro Fungus
dialogues.text: Yes, but I know their "end." I will explain it to you along the way.

talks.objective: Head to the place where the "end" awaits

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: There's something that I'm very concerned about.

choices.text: Are you talking about that crystal?

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: Yes. I didn't mention it just now, but do you remember when I told you that the power in the crystal is very similar to mine, yet also different?

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: The elemental power inside the crystal is completely identical to that of the Fungus.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: What!?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: There's a connection between the crystal and the Fungus...

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: Exactly. The prophecy that it mentioned was probably an agreement that I made with an elemental life-form that once represented its race.

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: I had to deal with the forbidden knowledge to save their homeland. The process, however, took away some of my memories.

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: That sequence of events would explain the persistent feeling that I had unfinished business.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Makes sense... Too bad it's unable to tell us more.

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: Yeah, I've been trying to think of a place that fits the description of its homeland, but I'm unable to come up with anything.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: We'll just have to continue investigating.

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: Agreed. I really want to send them home, so they won't have to wander around anymore.

choices.text: Are you talking about your fuzzy memories?

dialogues.speaker: Elemental Being: Floating Hydro Fungus
dialogues.text: As I expected, it's the last of my kind that I'm aware of.

dialogues.speaker: Elemental Being: Floating Hydro Fungus
dialogues.text: So it wasn't able to make it to the end. If only it could have held on just a little longer...

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: I hope that you will be free of this pain after returning home.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Just thinking about how many elemental life-forms have turned into Tumors of the Withering makes Paimon sad.

dialogues.speaker: Elemental Being: Floating Hydro Fungus
dialogues.text: It's okay. As long as elemental power still exists, then we will still be around.

dialogues.speaker: Elemental Being: Floating Hydro Fungus
dialogues.text: An external form is but a gift of time. Through "growth" comes change, and even abandonment of previous forms. However, our true nature is not so easily affected.

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: It wouldn't have come to this if we were able to cure them earlier...

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: But I will cure all of them... even if it's just for the sake of the rainforest and all the life-forms that live in it.

dialogues.speaker: Elemental Being: Floating Hydro Fungus
dialogues.text: Thank you, Lord of Dendro. It was a wise choice for us to place our trust in you and wait.

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: Hold on. I think I got something.

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: ...Oh, I see. Okay, I understand. Thank you so much.

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: So, they found a Fungus that matches the description I gave them. It's currently unconscious.

dialogues.speaker: Elemental Being: Floating Hydro Fungus
dialogues.text: It must be in a similar situation as I was. We should hurry and go take a look.

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: Okay, follow me.

talks.objective: Defeat the opponents blocking your path

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: We're close now. It's just a little further inside.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: But there are so many Fungi here. They're probably all ordinary Fungi, right?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yeah, they won't be happy to see us.

response.speaker: Elemental Being: Floating Hydro Fungus
response.text: No fighting. These are all its family.

response.speaker: Elemental Being: Floating Hydro Fungus
response.text: Although we belong to different species, we've spent a long time living among the Fungi. They are very important to us.

response.speaker: Elemental Being: Floating Hydro Fungus
response.text: They can be reasonable as long as we try to communicate.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: What should we do? You're the only one who can make it through, right?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: But you'll need Nahida's power if you want to save that Fungus.

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: I've got an idea. Can you teach me how to change into a Fungus?

response.speaker: Elemental Being: Floating Hydro Fungus
response.text: You want to transform into a Fungus? But we don't have time for growth...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Nahida is a god. Changing into a Fungus should be a piece of cake for her.

response.speaker: Elemental Being: Floating Hydro Fungus
response.text: Even gods can't bend the laws of time so easily.

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: Then we'll have to enter with the risk of being noticed. We may not be able to avoid a fight.

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: But if spending some of my power will guarantee the safety of you and its family, then I am willing to try.

response.speaker: Elemental Being: Floating Hydro Fungus
response.text: Alright. You have great elemental power, so you may be able to do it.

response.speaker: Elemental Being: Floating Hydro Fungus
response.text: You will have to use power equal to that which is required to break through the limitations of time.

response.speaker: Elemental Being: Floating Hydro Fungus
response.text: I will lend you the relevant knowledge that I have. It should make your transformation process a little easier.

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: Alright, I'm ready. Changing into a Fungus should be quite an interesting experience.

response.speaker: Elemental Being: Floating Hydro Fungus
response.text: Lord of Dendro, this is nothing to joke about. I am extremely serious about this.

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: Hmm? As am I. I'm not joking at all.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Alright, alright, let's not get hung up here. If it's really possible to turn into a Fungus, then why don't we give it a try now?

response.speaker: Elemental Being: Floating Hydro Fungus
response.text: Okay. Good luck, Lord of Dendro.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Wow! You really turned into a Fungus!

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: It's actually not too bad. My perspective in this form isn't much different from usual.

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: The unconscious Fungus is just below here. Can you all help me determine which one it is?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh, how do we do that?

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: I'll get close to them while you make your way over from above.

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: You should be able to identify them using Elemental Sight since they're elemental life-forms.

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: Then, all you have to do is repeat the correct answer in your mind. As long as I'm able to see you, then I'll be able to hear your answer.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Okay, got it!

response.speaker: Elemental Being: Floating Hydro Fungus
response.text: Let me lure away the Fungi up top and make way for you.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #Alright, good luck, Nahida. Let's go, {NICKNAME}!

choices.text: We won't be able to avoid a fight.

dialogues.speaker: Elemental Being: Floating Hydro Fungus
dialogues.text: Amazing. With such skills, you all would've definitely been able to find a way to survive the apocalypse.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hey, Paimon has been meaning to ask — you all didn't originally look like this, did you?

dialogues.speaker: Elemental Being: Floating Hydro Fungus
dialogues.text: No, we didn't. The appearance of our kind will change according to the environment.

dialogues.speaker: Elemental Being: Floating Hydro Fungus
dialogues.text: After communicating with various living organisms in Sumeru, we discovered that Fungi are the life-form most adapted to live in these lands.

dialogues.speaker: Elemental Being: Floating Hydro Fungus
dialogues.text: Thus, we gradually took the form of Fungi and became a part of their group.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: It's hard to believe that's even possible!

dialogues.speaker: Elemental Being: Floating Hydro Fungus
dialogues.text: The most important instinct any life-form possesses is adapting to the environment. I don't think that should surprise you, Paimon.

dialogues.speaker: Elemental Being: Floating Hydro Fungus
dialogues.text: Your hand is shaped like that for a reason — so you are able to grip and use tools more easily.

dialogues.speaker: Elemental Being: Floating Hydro Fungus
dialogues.text: The reason why Fungi absorb elemental power is to blend with the environment and fend off natural predators.

dialogues.speaker: Elemental Being: Floating Hydro Fungus
dialogues.text: We are Dendro life-forms, one of the most ancient life-forms in this land. That is why we are so adaptable.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: So you mean... If Paimon wanted to, Paimon could change into a different form as well?

dialogues.speaker: Elemental Being: Floating Hydro Fungus
dialogues.text: Not as freely, I'm afraid. You would require a long time to make that happen.

dialogues.speaker: Elemental Being: Floating Hydro Fungus
dialogues.text: Although this is common sense to us, it is still extremely difficult to explain. Hmm... Putting it as simply as possible, changing form requires energy, and energy comes with time.

dialogues.speaker: Elemental Being: Floating Hydro Fungus
dialogues.text: You cannot make a sprout grow into a giant tree instantly, nor can you force a tree to bear fruit overnight.

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: I see. Humans have a term for this, it's called "growth."

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ahh, you're so smart, Nahida! Paimon gets it now!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Seems like it's pretty good at coming up with metaphors as well...

dialogues.speaker: Elemental Being: Floating Hydro Fungus
dialogues.text: "Growth"... I see. Yes, then this is what you would call growth.

dialogues.speaker: Elemental Being: Floating Hydro Fungus
dialogues.text: A most beautiful word. I shall enjoy it more as we walk.

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: (There's a Fungus on patrol in the center there. It looks pretty vigilant, so I'd better go around it.)

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: (It seems they didn't notice me.)

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: (It seems that Fungus won't be moving for the moment. I should hurry and make my way through.)

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: (This is the spot. There are several Fungi here.)

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: #(I'll hide and wait for {NICKNAME} to catch up.)

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: (Why is it reacting like that?)

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: (Uh oh, the Fungus on patrol noticed me.)

response.speaker: Black Screen
response.text: The planned infiltration of the habitat failed because you were detected...

talks.objective: Defeat the opponents blocking your path

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: (Ah, so this is the one. Understood.)

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: Nahida uses her elemental power on the Fungus.

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: Seeing their companion regain consciousness, the nearby Fungi lower their guard against you.

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: You successfully meet up with Nahida, and she returns to her original form.

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: *panting*... Whew...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Nahida, what's wrong?

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: I never knew that it was so tiring to change forms like that.

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: I even used the techniques that it taught me... Seems like its warnings were not unfounded.

dialogues.speaker: Elemental Being: Floating Hydro Fungus
dialogues.text: The power of time accumulates slowly and goes unnoticed. A great price is to be paid if you wish to perform drastic changes instantly.

dialogues.speaker: Elemental Being: Floating Hydro Fungus
dialogues.text: Thank you for everything you've done. All seems to have gone according to plan. Now we simply wait for it to wake up.

dialogues.speaker: Elemental Being: Floating Anemo Fungus
dialogues.text: Who... are you?

dialogues.speaker: Elemental Being: Floating Anemo Fungus
dialogues.text: I apologize. Language... is not... easy. Need... long... time...

dialogues.speaker: Elemental Being: Floating Hydro Fungus
dialogues.text: It's okay, I have good news. Let me explain it to you the Fungi way.

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: A while later...

dialogues.speaker: Elemental Being: Floating Anemo Fungus
dialogues.text: Apocalypse... ended. Go home... now?

dialogues.speaker: Elemental Being: Floating Hydro Fungus
dialogues.text: Yes. Unfortunately, I've forgotten where home is. I was hoping you still remembered.

dialogues.speaker: Elemental Being: Floating Anemo Fungus
dialogues.text: I... remember.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Really? That's great!

dialogues.speaker: Elemental Being: Floating Anemo Fungus
dialogues.text: Home... Dendro Dragon.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Dendro Dragon?

dialogues.speaker: Elemental Being: Floating Hydro Fungus
dialogues.text: Dendro Dragon... Ah... Yes! The Dendro Dragon!

dialogues.speaker: Elemental Being: Floating Hydro Fungus
dialogues.text: I'm sorry, I just got so excited. I've probably never expressed such emotions before. But yes, our home is the Dendro Dragon.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: W—Wait a minute, Paimon's confused! Do you mean the Dendro Dragon as in an elemental dragon? Like Dvalin?

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: Yes. They're both dragons but Apep, the Dendro Dragon, has been around for longer and has accumulated dense elemental power...

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: But I don't quite understand — why would you say that your homeland is a dragon?

dialogues.speaker: Elemental Being: Floating Hydro Fungus
dialogues.text: Because we live inside the Dendro Dragon.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Uh...

dialogues.speaker: Elemental Being: Floating Anemo Fungus
dialogues.text: The Dendro Dragon... Inside... Very big... Mountains... water... trees... us.

dialogues.speaker: Elemental Being: Floating Hydro Fungus
dialogues.text: There is an entire world inside the Dendro Dragon's body. The Dendro Dragon nurtured the earliest life-forms, and protected us inside of itself.

dialogues.speaker: Elemental Being: Floating Hydro Fungus
dialogues.text: It once told us in a majestic voice that once we've finally matured, we'd be able to start life in a new world.

dialogues.speaker: Elemental Being: Floating Hydro Fungus
dialogues.text: However, that day never came. Our homeland was the greatest place there ever was before the apocalypse arrived.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Paimon's still confused...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Is it like... Dendro Slimes giving birth to smaller slimes?

dialogues.speaker: Elemental Being: Floating Hydro Fungus
dialogues.text: Yes, a very good example. It appears that you're much smarter than Paimon. The only difference is that the Dendro Dragon is much, much larger than any Dendro Slime.

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: Wait... Then if that's the case... Doesn't that imply that Apep has also been contaminated by forbidden knowledge?

dialogues.speaker: Elemental Being: Floating Hydro Fungus
dialogues.text: Yes, that is correct.

dialogues.speaker: Elemental Being: Floating Hydro Fungus
dialogues.text: What has suddenly made you look so worried, Lord of Dendro? I haven't seen this expression on you before.

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: Apep is the most adaptable life-form in the world. The forbidden knowledge should've become a part of its body a long time ago.

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: Which means that if all the forbidden knowledge has been eliminated...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Then a big void will also form inside the dragon!

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: I'm afraid so... Its body and soul have probably been in terrible shape for some time now.

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: No wonder I haven't seen Apep for so long. But how did it get contaminated...? Was it due to the destruction of King Deshret's civilization?

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: Hmm... But anyway, Apep disappeared and has been gone ever since that time. It's been enduring unimaginable pain all the while... It's probably in pain as we speak...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: So saving the Dendro Dragon is the important thing you need to do?

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: Yes! How could I have forgotten!?

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: If the Dendro Dragon fails to hang on, the elemental power inside it will no longer be able to maintain its form, and will all be dispersed.

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: Dendro elemental power of that concentration will cause the rainforest to overgrow...

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: Giant trees will completely block out the sun... Plants and humans will fight over oxygen... Sumeru will no longer be suitable for sustaining life!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Nahida, get ahold of yourself.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hey, what about the crystal? Why don't you show it to them and see if they know anything about it?

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: *sigh* Yes, I'm sorry... You're right. We don't have time to panic.

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: Have you two ever seen anything like this before?

dialogues.speaker: Elemental Being: Floating Anemo Fungus
dialogues.text: No.

dialogues.speaker: Elemental Being: Floating Hydro Fungus
dialogues.text: Its power feels very familiar... like something from our homeland, but I don't know what it is.

dialogues.speaker: Elemental Being: Floating Hydro Fungus
dialogues.text: I'm sorry, our memories aren't very reliable.

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: It's okay. I'll contact my helpers just as I did before and see if they can locate your other family members.

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: I'm counting on you all, your info is crucial to us now.

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: Let's wait for their reply again. Though I know waiting can feel unbearable at a time like this...

dialogues.speaker: Elemental Being: Floating Anemo Fungus
dialogues.text: Thank... you... Family... bringing... fruit.

dialogues.speaker: Elemental Being: Floating Hydro Fungus
dialogues.text: I explained to them that you aren't hostile. After seeing you save it, its family is very grateful to you.

dialogues.speaker: Elemental Being: Floating Anemo Fungus
dialogues.text: Go home... Leave... Hard decision... Don't know.

dialogues.speaker: Elemental Being: Floating Anemo Fungus
dialogues.text: They are... weak... I... Worry.

dialogues.speaker: Elemental Being: Floating Anemo Fungus
dialogues.text: If waiting... Then... I hope...

dialogues.speaker: Elemental Being: Floating Hydro Fungus
dialogues.text: Don't worry, I understand what you are trying to say.

dialogues.speaker: Elemental Being: Floating Hydro Fungus
dialogues.text: Family is very important to us, no matter when we were actually family. It has done a lot to protect this territory and can't help but worry now that it's about to leave.

dialogues.speaker: Elemental Being: Floating Hydro Fungus
dialogues.text: Can you do one last thing for it while we wait?

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: Of course. I can relate to how it's feeling.

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: I need to organize my thoughts as well...

dialogues.speaker: Elemental Being: Floating Anemo Fungus
dialogues.text: Thank you... Thank you.

dialogues.speaker: Elemental Being: Floating Anemo Fungus
dialogues.text: Tend... Soil... Food.

dialogues.speaker: Elemental Being: Floating Anemo Fungus
dialogues.text: Don't like... Plant... Invasion.

dialogues.speaker: Elemental Being: Floating Hydro Fungus
dialogues.text: There are two things that it wants you to do. One is to look after the land that the food is grown in, and the other is to drive away the plants that are trying to invade the area.

dialogues.speaker: Elemental Being: Floating Anemo Fungus
dialogues.text: Soil... there. First... seed... here.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Paimon understood that! No need to translate! We'll take care of it right away!

dialogues.speaker: Elemental Being: Floating Hydro Fungus
dialogues.text: Hmm, I think we may have a different understanding of "carrying" someone.

dialogues.speaker: Elemental Being: Floating Hydro Fungus
dialogues.text: No matter whether it's tired or not, my child is always happy when I put it on my back and give it a ride.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Child? You mean the Fungi we ran into earlier?

dialogues.speaker: Elemental Being: Floating Hydro Fungus
dialogues.text: Yes. One was my friend, and the other was my child.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Why can't your kid speak?

dialogues.speaker: Elemental Being: Floating Hydro Fungus
dialogues.text: Because it's just a Fungus. I don't want my presence to change or affect the original state of the Fungi species here.

dialogues.speaker: Elemental Being: Floating Hydro Fungus
dialogues.text: However, it is slightly different from an ordinary Fungus. It seems to understand some human language, so I gave it a name.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh, then it must be a really cute name!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: You know, like Bongo-Head!

dialogues.speaker: Elemental Being: Floating Hydro Fungus
dialogues.text: Hmm, you have an odd taste for names.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh? Paimon thinks that name is great!

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: Strange and cute at the same time. It's a name only Paimon would be able to come up with.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hehe, that's right.

dialogues.speaker: Elemental Being: Floating Hydro Fungus
dialogues.text: The name I came up with was not as creative as Paimon's. I learned it from an adventurer. It's...

dialogues.speaker: Elemental Being: Floating Hydro Fungus
dialogues.text: Its name is...

dialogues.speaker: Elemental Being: Floating Hydro Fungus
dialogues.text: I'm sorry, but I've forgotten... *sigh* Seems like I've forgotten many important things.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Don't worry. You can try and remember it on the way.

dialogues.speaker: Elemental Being: Floating Hydro Fungus
dialogues.text: Yes, I must remember it before I return. It's just as important as my homeland.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: It's... The Withering!

dialogues.speaker: Elemental Being: Floating Hydro Fungus
dialogues.text: Yes, I have heard humans also call it that before.

dialogues.speaker: Elemental Being: Floating Hydro Fungus
dialogues.text: It's the last form we take when we are at the end of our life.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Uh, Paimon doesn't understand...

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: It's trying to say that when they've suffered enough and reached the end of their life, they become a Tumor of the Withering.

dialogues.speaker: Elemental Being: Floating Hydro Fungus
dialogues.text: Yes. I would have also suffered the same fate if it wasn't for the Lord of Dendro's help.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: So this is how "The Withering" is formed...?

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: Previous research has revealed that forbidden knowledge is the root cause of The Withering.

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: But even if forbidden knowledge has been completely removed, its influence still remains, which is why The Withering remains even after forbidden knowledge has disappeared.

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: They've been tormented by forbidden knowledge for a long time. It's understandable that they will eventually become The Withering.

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: But what a sad and pitiful end...

dialogues.speaker: Elemental Being: Floating Hydro Fungus
dialogues.text: When I left my homeland, flowers like these filled the fields. Each bloom represented an individual life.

dialogues.speaker: Elemental Being: Floating Hydro Fungus
dialogues.text: They grew in the pristine lakes, in the fertile soil, in my home, and in the homes of my friends...

dialogues.speaker: Elemental Being: Floating Hydro Fungus
dialogues.text: They grew everywhere. Until the world suddenly lost all its color and became tainted and murky.

dialogues.speaker: Elemental Being: Floating Hydro Fungus
dialogues.text: But it's alright. Our life essence — elemental power — still resides in this flower.

dialogues.speaker: Elemental Being: Floating Hydro Fungus
dialogues.text: After an adventurer clears The Withering, I will quietly draw near the area. If I can sense the elemental power of my companions, then I take them with me.

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: But that would mean the effects of forbidden knowledge could've...

dialogues.speaker: Elemental Being: Floating Hydro Fungus
dialogues.text: It's okay. That's not important anymore. I just hope that they can all make it back home.

dialogues.speaker: Elemental Being: Floating Hydro Fungus
dialogues.text: It's not right to leave them to simply perish in the open like this.

dialogues.speaker: Elemental Being: Floating Hydro Fungus
dialogues.text: Now that we finally have the chance to return home, each one I manage to bring back will make me that much happier.

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: I understand. Just leave it to us.

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: So you're worried about me...

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: Hehe, it's fine. Forbidden knowledge doesn't exist anymore.

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: It's natural to want to be over-cautious when dealing with a highly venomous snake, but when all that's left is its skeleton, there's nothing to worry about.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: ...If you say so.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Uh, Paimon doesn't get what you two are talking about, but we're all ready to go now, right?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Then let's do this! We've dealt with The Withering countless times already!

choices.text: This is a product of forbidden knowledge, after all.

dialogues.speaker: Elemental Being: Floating Anemo Fungus
dialogues.text: Thank you... Lord of Dendro. Family... happy.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: You really like them, don't you?

dialogues.speaker: Elemental Being: Floating Anemo Fungus
dialogues.text: Family... like. Do you... not like... your family?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ahh, that's not what Paimon meant. It's just that you guys aren't actually the same species.

dialogues.speaker: Elemental Being: Floating Anemo Fungus
dialogues.text: Does not matter. Family... likes... me. I... like... family.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Uh, Paimon doesn't quite understand...

dialogues.speaker: Elemental Being: Floating Hydro Fungus
dialogues.text: What it's trying to say is that as long as family members get along well, then nothing else matters.

dialogues.speaker: Elemental Being: Floating Hydro Fungus
dialogues.text: You place importance on appearances, but we do not. We find the experiences, knowledge, and connections we've made to be more important.

dialogues.speaker: Elemental Being: Floating Hydro Fungus
dialogues.text: These are all things that are more reliable than mere external appearances... These are the fruits of time, and the essence of what it means to grow.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh, Paimon gets it now. Looks can always change, so what's inside of us is more important.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: It wouldn't matter! Paimon would still be able to recognize you right away.

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: Oh? Hmm... Understood. Thank you.

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: Still nothing new from the forest. Seems like we won't be able to find your other family members for now.

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: Hmm, it appears we are out of leads to follow... And if no one knows how this crystal works, then Apep may be in danger.

response.speaker: Elemental Being: Floating Anemo Fungus
response.text: Sorry.

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: It's okay, it isn't your fault. I don't think it's a coincidence that neither of you can remember anything about the crystal.

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: Maybe it's because the crystal has a very close connection to forbidden knowledge which causes memories of it to be unclear.

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: And if that's the case, finding the other Fungi still wouldn't help us at all.

response.speaker: Elemental Being: Floating Hydro Fungus
response.text: Hmm. The crystal and the apocalypse... The apocalypse and memories...

response.speaker: Elemental Being: Floating Hydro Fungus
response.text: Lord of Dendro, do you still remember the prophecy?

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: Mm-hmm, I do. What about it?

response.speaker: Elemental Being: Floating Hydro Fungus
response.text: The prophecy is a story that connects events of the past and the future. A family member once said that the apocalypse is a part of us and that there is value in preserving it.

response.speaker: Elemental Being: Floating Hydro Fungus
response.text: The rest of the family did not approve of its opinion at the time, so it left.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Preserving the apocalypse? Do you mean that there's still some that hasn't been eliminated?

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: That's not very likely. The power of Irminsul covers every inch of the land.

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: Did the prophecy say where that family member went?

response.speaker: Elemental Being: Floating Hydro Fungus
response.text: To the limitless depths east of Sumeru. A murky place that no one can return from.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: The Chasm.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yeah, that must be The Chasm, right? But what is it doing there...?

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: Hmm... it's impossible to preserve forbidden knowledge. But...

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: What if it can be converted to a different form?

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: I'm sorry if I'm suddenly not making any sense. However, I do think it's possible.

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: Follow me. I'll explain it once we find that elemental life-form.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Paimon would still follow you around. Wait... would you not be able to recognize Paimon?

talks.objective: Seek out the other elemental life-form
Try to infiltrate the Fungi habitat
Approach from the other side and activate Elemental Sight
Heal the elemental life-form and speak with it

dialogues.speaker: Elemental Being: Floating Hydro Fungus
dialogues.text: I'm moved that they were so worried about me.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Whew, that should be all of 'em. That wasn't too tough!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Nahida, are you feeling better?

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: Yeah, I've calmed down now. But it doesn't seem like there's too much we can do until we receive some new leads.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Can you tell us about the Dendro Dragon? We don't know anything about it. Who is it, and what does it have to do with King Deshret?

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: Well, the history of dragons starts from the very beginning of Teyvat.

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: Sumeru was Apep's territory. In those days, the lush rainforest covered the entire nation.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh? So there was no desert back then?

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: Not at first. That came when a giant spike fell from the sky, turning a huge section of the rainforest into sand.

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: In an attempt to adapt to its new environment, Apep changed color from the emerald green of the forest to the yellow of the sand.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: No wonder those two elemental life-forms are always talking about the importance of "adapting"...

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: Apep has always seen itself as the master of Sumeru and has refused to recognize the new order that was established. Even now, it probably still holds great hostility toward the gods.

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: However, powerless against the power in the sky and then the forbidden knowledge many millennia later, it's been unable to stir up any trouble.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: I thought the gods and dragons were on good terms?

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: Conflicts between the two sides are destined to continue until a balance can be found.

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: As far as I know, Apep had been slumbering in the desert, and King Deshret had taken a great interest in it. Maybe this is why Apep was contaminated.

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: I'm not sure what may have led it to become involved, but rescuing it is definitely our top priority right now.

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: The crystal that I have in my possession is probably the key that links the two matters together.

talks.objective: Return and speak to the elemental life-form

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hey, isn't that Nahida?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Nahida! Paimon didn't think we'd run into you here.

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: Oh, hey there. It's been a while, hasn't it? What have you two been up to?

choices.text: Same old, same old. Adventuring and stuff...

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: Hehe, seems like you've been enjoying yourselves.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: How about you? What are you up to now?

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: I'm just out looking for some leads while getting some fresh air.

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: I noticed that I have some blurry memories after saving Irminsul.

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: I almost feel like there's still something extremely important I need to do... But I can't remember what it is.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hmm, why is that?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: (It's probably the effects of Irminsul...)

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Don't worry, we'll help you remember.

choices.text: Feel free to fill us in.

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: Thank you so much. Since you're willing to help, I have something I'd like to show you.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oooh, it's beautiful! It looks like it's filled with some kind of power.

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: Mm-hmm. I found it in the Sanctuary of Surasthana, but I have no recollection of it whatsoever.

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: It's filled with pure elemental power that is quite similar to mine, but yet it's also a little different...

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: It's very likely that it's connected to my foggy memory, but I can't figure out what it is.

choices.text: (It's most likely something that Greater Lord Rukkhadevata left behind...)

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #{NICKNAME}, do you have any ideas?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hmm. You know, Nahida, we just happen to be going on an adventure right now. If we find anything, we'll be sure to let you know right away.

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: Thanks, you two. I didn't mean to trouble you again.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Don't mention it! Besides, it seems you've got a lot on your mind, and we'd like to help.

response.speaker: Layth
response.text: Hey, get out! You shouldn't be around here!

response.speaker: Layth
response.text: I'm sorry, Lesser Lord Kusanali. Fungi don't usually come near this place.

response.speaker: Layth
response.text: Last warning, get out before I kick you out! You hear!?

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: Hang on... I think it's trying to tell us something.

response.speaker: Layth
response.text: But Great Dendro Archon, it's a monster.

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: Please, don't worry.

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: Hmm... I think I understand.

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: Seems that it wants us to follow it.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: You could understand it?

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: Mm-hmm. Even though different creatures have varying habits and ways of communicating, the emotions we experience are all the same.

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: I can feel its anxiety and fear. It's in dire need of our help.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Well, Fungi are kinda cute, but...

choices.text: The usual... Mining, fishing, Genius Invokation TCG, and catching Crystalflies.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Bongo-Head is a really nice Fungus, you know.

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: I was confident that I knew of all the creatures in Teyvat. Even if there are ones I've never seen with my own eyes, I thought I possessed all the relevant knowledge about them.

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: However, even if I were to lay out the traits of all elemental life-forms, you don't seem to match any of them.

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: What are you? And where did you come from?

dialogues.speaker: Elemental Being: Floating Hydro Fungus
dialogues.text: I come from an ancient race. We have existed for a very long time, possibly longer than any records in existence.

dialogues.speaker: Elemental Being: Floating Hydro Fungus
dialogues.text: My home was filled with flowing water and great mountains. Lush grass covered the land, and my family and I lived in bliss and happiness.

dialogues.speaker: Elemental Being: Floating Hydro Fungus
dialogues.text: Until... the "apocalypse" came and changed my home forever...

dialogues.speaker: Elemental Being: Floating Hydro Fungus
dialogues.text: A horrifying power consumed all there was... The seeds of catastrophe nested and grew inside of us... Twisting and warping us, causing us to lose control.

dialogues.speaker: Elemental Being: Floating Hydro Fungus
dialogues.text: We were victims of the apocalypse, yet in time, we also became the apocalypse itself.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: The "apocalypse"?

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: I'm not sure what it means either. It sounds like some kind of old fable.

dialogues.speaker: Elemental Being: Floating Hydro Fungus
dialogues.text: It's a long and complicated story. It will take me some time to explain it clearly.

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: Don't worry, we'll listen. Please continue.

dialogues.speaker: Elemental Being: Floating Hydro Fungus
dialogues.text: I was lucky and managed to survive. Afterward, I left with some of my family and came to Sumeru to search for a way to rescue my homeland.

dialogues.speaker: Elemental Being: Floating Hydro Fungus
dialogues.text: We came in contact with many species and learned from their cultures and knowledge, hoping to understand the truth behind the apocalypse.

dialogues.speaker: Elemental Being: Floating Hydro Fungus
dialogues.text: We later found out that humans know the power of the apocalypse, and refer to it as "forbidden knowledge."

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Forbidden knowledge...!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Your home was destroyed by forbidden knowledge? Does that mean you're from the desert?

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: It said that they are looking for a way to save their homeland, but the catastrophe of the desert should've ended a long time ago.

dialogues.speaker: Elemental Being: Floating Hydro Fungus
dialogues.text: The Lord of Dendro is correct. We are not from the desert. I would very much like to tell you the location of my homeland... But unfortunately, I've forgotten.

dialogues.speaker: Elemental Being: Floating Hydro Fungus
dialogues.text: That may sound a little odd... As it is very important to both me and my family.

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: Yes, how could you forget?

dialogues.speaker: Elemental Being: Floating Hydro Fungus
dialogues.text: I am a life-form that was contaminated by the apocalypse. A part of my knowledge and memory was taken away as the contamination inside of me was purged.

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: Ah, I get it now... So the void of elemental power was left behind from when the forbidden knowledge was purged.

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: I'm sorry. I hadn't considered that kind of possibility...

dialogues.speaker: Elemental Being: Floating Hydro Fungus
dialogues.text: That's okay. Lord of Dendro, there is no need to apologize. Without your help, I would've lost more than just my knowledge and memory.

dialogues.speaker: Elemental Being: Floating Hydro Fungus
dialogues.text: And not only did you save me, but you've also already rid the world of the remaining forbidden knowledge, right?

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: That's right. The forbidden knowledge is no more, and your homeland should be safe now.

dialogues.speaker: Elemental Being: Floating Hydro Fungus
dialogues.text: My home... should be safe now. We can go home...

dialogues.speaker: Elemental Being: Floating Hydro Fungus
dialogues.text: For the longest time, this moment has only seemed like a dream... I never knew it would become a reality so quickly.

dialogues.speaker: Elemental Being: Floating Hydro Fungus
dialogues.text: I was unable to fulfill our calling. I never found a way to save my homeland, and I have even forgotten where it is...

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: It's not your fault. You've already done everything you can.

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: Every species paid a grave price in the fight against forbidden knowledge. This is not a responsibility you should carry on your own.

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: You mentioned that there were other survivors besides yourself. Where are they? Maybe they'll remember.

dialogues.speaker: Elemental Being: Floating Hydro Fungus
dialogues.text: The apocalypse put us through immense pain. Many of my family members have already met their end. I'm not sure who else is still alive...

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: Don't worry, I should be able to find them. Just leave it to me.

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: My familiars will take the rainforest, and as for the city... There are a few nice kids who should be willing to help.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Your familiars?

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: Mm-hmm, they're a group of lovely little creatures. They're just a bit timid around strangers.

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: I'll leave the rainforest to the Aranara, and as for the city... There are a few nice kids that should be willing to help.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh yeah! They'll give us a hand!

dialogues.speaker: Elemental Being: Floating Anemo Fungus
dialogues.text: Leave... worried... Want to stay.

dialogues.speaker: Elemental Being: Floating Anemo Fungus
dialogues.text: Preparation... almost... complete.

dialogues.speaker: Elemental Being: Floating Hydro Fungus
dialogues.text: Thank you so much for your willingness to help. In the meantime, I'd like to tell it the things we experienced on the way here.

dialogues.speaker: Elemental Being: Floating Hydro Fungus
dialogues.text: Sharing knowledge is a habit of ours.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Although they all look about the same, some Fungi are friendly, while others are super aggressive and attack anyone they see.

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: It can't be helped. Perhaps in their eyes, humans are like fierce "monsters" as well.

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: After all, they can't distinguish which human behaviors are hostile or not, and it'd already be too late for them once humans have drawn their weapons.

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: Hence why they tend to strike first, rather than waiting.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: That's not too different from how humans think sometimes...

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: That's what I meant by shared emotions.

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: (It seems to be anxious. Let's follow it and see where it leads.)

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: (It seems to be anxious and afraid.)

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: (Hmm? There's something strange about this Fungus...)

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: (I can sense its excitement from seeing its fellow Fungus wake back up.)

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: (It seems to have let out a long sigh of relief...)

dialogues.speaker: Elemental Being: Floating Hydro Fungus
dialogues.text: The road here is a little rough. I'll lead the way.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Don't worry — Paimon can handle any road!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #Wahh! Enemies! You're up, {NICKNAME}!

dialogues.speaker: Elemental Being: Floating Hydro Fungus
dialogues.text: (No matter how long it's been, it still looks like it had suddenly frozen in place.)

dialogues.speaker: Elemental Being: Floating Hydro Fungus
dialogues.text: Yes, this way. We're almost there.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Come back! They'll spot you if you keep going that way!

dialogues.speaker: Elemental Being: Floating Hydro Fungus
dialogues.text: (The Lord of Dendro is a kind god, just as described in the prophecy.)

dialogues.speaker: Elemental Being: Floating Anemo Fungus
dialogues.text: (Time... short... long... Go home...)

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: We've planted all the seeds. It's time to handle the invading plant life.

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: (It's happy because it found some delicious fruit.)

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: (It looks like it's in a good mood, and is waiting for another Fungus.)

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: (It looks really sleepy. Why doesn't it go to sleep?)

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: (It looks like it's very curious about us.)

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: (It appears to be encouraging itself. Is it about to face some kind of formidable foe?)

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: (It seems to be welcoming us as guests.)
